newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: EU urges free movement of aid in Zaire.
newsitem.headline: EU urges free movement of aid in Zaire.

text.p: The European Union on Saturday urged the warring factions in Zaire to allow the free movement of humanitarian aid to thousands of refugees.

"It is with great concern that the European Union has learned about the rapidly deteriorating situation in Kisangani," Dutch Foreign Minister Hans van Mierlo told a news conference during a two-day informal gathering of the bloc's 15 foreign ministers in the central Netherlands.
"Once more this means that large groups of refugees have to move further without any assistance of any kind being able to reach them.
"This means further suffering for the Zairean population," van Mierlo said.
"The EU calls on all parties to the conflict in eastern Zaire to respect the lives of both refugees and Zaireans."

"As the largest provider of humanitarian aid (to Zaire), the EU urges all the parties involved to safeguard the humanitarian corridors...in order to enable the delivery of the humanitarian assistance that is so urgently needed," van Mierlo said.
Rebels in the African nation earlier captured Zaire's third largest city of Kisangani, dealing a severe blow to President Mobutu Seke Seko's government.
